Final answer (raw-counts, locked-in approach): Pearson r = 0.0617 (r = 0.06169702), computed over n = 19,942 protein-coding genes, using per-gene arithmetic mean of raw batch-corrected read counts across the 151 CD4 columns, correlated with gene Length (bp, joined by Geneid).

- n used: 19,942 protein-coding genes; CD4 samples: 151 columns (annotation celltype=='CD4' ≡ matrix CD4-suffix columns); 1,518 protein-coding genes with mean=0 across CD4 were retained per the approved plan.
- Executed analysis script: /workspace/analysis_cd4_length_corr.py (also saved /workspace/result_summary.csv).
- Join/filter confirmation: matrix row Geneids (59,453, unique) exactly equal GeneMetaInfo Geneid set (1:1, no missing); CD4 column set from annotation equals the CD4-suffix matrix columns (151 = 151); protein_coding = 19,942, all Length > 0 with no NA; no NaN in the CD4 expression subset — all matched the plan exactly.
- Documented side-note (not the reported answer): r rises to 0.3175 under log1p(mean) and is 0.0528 if the 1,518 zero-expression genes are excluded — confirming the raw-counts, full-gene-set choice was consequential.
